title: Kind predicates derived from the archetype

story.i_want_to: every 'is this implement' check to ask the spec's archetype
story.so_that: a new :build spec is treated as claim-holding everywhere without a code search

rationale: DispatchLedger.implement_kind? (dispatch_ledger.ex:869-874, nil counts as implement), budget_keys (dispatch_payload.ex:443-444), fill/3's kind default (:117-131) and the runner-side prefix exemption all special-case the kind string.

acceptance_criteria.description: Spec.holds_claim?(kind) replaces implement_kind?; budget_keys, fill/3's default and accepted_session's default kind come from the spec.
A property test over every registry kind plus nil and an unknown kind shows the old and new predicates agree.
An unknown kind fails closed: it holds no claim and gets no budget.

test_cases.name: unknown kind
steps: ask holds_claim? and budget_keys for an unknown kind

technical_notes: The runner-side prefix exemption moves in US-48.8 with the contract change.
